[S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll. dhammupalakkhaṇa:
1dhamma
m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. mfn., [pp of *√gup; S. gupta], 1. protected; defended, kept safe; guarded; controlled; Abh 754 (rakkhitaṃ gopitaṃ ~aṃ); M I 503,.15 (cakkhuṃ … tathāgatassa dantaṃ ~aṃ rakkhitaṃ saṃvutaṃ); S IV 117,.17 (~āni dvārāni surakkhitāni ahesuṃ); Dhp 36 (cittaṃ ~aṃ sukhāvahaṃ); 315 (nagaraṃ yathā paccantaṃ ~aṃ santarabāhiraṃ); Ja II 33,25* (tay’ ajja ~ā viharemu divasaṃ); IV 487,7* (amhehi ~ā anusāsa rajjaṃ); V 213,20* (nivesanaṃ … pākārena paṇḍu-mayena ~aṃ); Sp 350,.12 (~e ṭhāne); Th-a I 242,.17 (cakkhudvārādīnaṃ °-ttā); — ifc see dhamma- (sv dhamma1); — 2. guarded, watchful; controlled, keeping a control; Vin I 195,.29 (dakkhissasi … dantaṃ ~aṃ yatindriyaṃ nāgaṃ) ≠ A II 38,.7; Sn 250 (sotesu ~o vijitindriyo care); Ap 313,.9 (sadā ~o); Nidd I 221,.5 (vācāyato ti yatto paṭiyatto ~o gopito rakkhito saṃvuto vūpasanto); Dhp-a IV 117,.3 (attanā va °-tāya attagutto); — 3. hidden, concealed; Abh 746 (gūḷho tu ~o); — 4. who protects, a defender, preserver; Dhp 257 (dhammassa ~o medhāvī dhammaṭṭho ti pavuccati; or gen. in sense of instr.; Dhp-a III 382,.10 : so dhammagutto dhammarakkhito dhammojapaññāya samannāgato); Vv 84:21 (ahaṃ hi yakkho kantāriyo vaṇṇupathamhi ~o; Vv-a 341,.9 : ~o ti gopako); — ifc see dhamma- (sv dhamma1); —      °-dvāra,   mfn., with means of access (of the sense-faculties) guarded, defended; controlled; D I 70,.7 foll. (kathaṃ ca … bhikkhu indriyesu ~o hoti …); M III 2,.14 (ehi tvaṃ bhikkhu indriyesu ~o hohi, cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā mā nimittaggāhī mā ’nuvyañjanaggāhī); Sn 413 (sapadānaṃ caramāno ~o susaṃvuto); Pv 38:43 (okkhittacakkhu satimā ~o susaṃvuto); Th 116 (cha phassāyatane hitvā ~o susaṃvuto); Dhs 1347 (katamā indriyesu ~-tā); Peṭ 148,.14; Kv 616,.6 (atthi gabbhaseyyāya … indriyesu ~-tā); Mil 343,5* (~ā susaṃvutā); Vism 19,.11; — neg. aguttadvāra, mfn., D III 213,.7 (indriyesu aguttadvāratā ca bhojane amattaññutā ca); M I 32,.10; S IV 119,.25 foll. (kittāvatā nu kho … aguttadvāro hotī ti …); It 23,.3; Ja III 532,.4; Dhs 1345; —       °-bhāsana,   n., private or confidential talk; Dhātup 578 (manta ~e); Sadd 539,.19 (manto ti ~aṃ); —      agutta,   mfn., 1. unprotected, unguarded; not controlled, not watched over; Vin I 284,.31 (saṅghassa bhaṇḍāgāre cīvaraṃ ~aṃ hoti); II 148,.21 (vihārā ~ā honti); S IV 70,.3 (cha-y-ime … phassāyatanā adantā ~ā arakkhitā asaṃvutā); A I 7,.3 (cittaṃ bhikkhave ~aṃ mahato anatthāya saṃvattatī ti); It 23,12* (cakkhu sotaṃ ca ghānaṃ ca jivhā kāyo tathā mano etāni yassa dvārāni ~āni ’dha bhikkhuno; It-a I 101,.12 foll. : yassa bhikkhuno etāni manachaṭṭhāni dvārāni sativossaggena pamādaṃ āpannattā satikavāṭena apihitāni); Ja IV 247,.5 (nagaraṃ ~aṃ); Vism 22,.1 (dvāraṃ pi ~aṃ hoti); Sp 388,.20 (yo pana saṅghiko dabbasambhāro ~o deve vassante temeti ātapena sukkhati); 778,.15 (seyyamattam eva nasseyya ṭhānassa ~-tāya); — 2. unguarded, unwatchful; not controlled; A I 281,1* (~aṃ cakkhusotasmiṃ indriyesu asaṃvutaṃ); —      sugutta,   mfn., well-guarded, well-defended; carefully watched over; Vin V 133,.5 (attano sīlakkhandho ~o hoti surakkhito); S IV 70,.13 (cha-y-ime … phassāyatanā sudantā ~ā …); It 24,11* (etāni yassa dvārāni ~āni ’dha bhikkhuno); Th 1141; Ja V 29,2* (mātā … ~ā, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee sugattā); Sp 1129,.28 (āraññakassa pana vihāro na ~o hoti); Spk I 321,.4 (Āḷavakassa pana vimānaṃ bhummaṭṭhaṃ ~aṃ pākāraparikkhittaṃ); — see also gopāyati, gopeti1, jigucchati.
tajjanī:
tajjanī
f. [S. tarjanī], the forefinger; Abh 266.
tajjayati:
tajjeti, ~ayati
(and tajjati), pr. 3 sg. ta(d)
demonstr. pronoun and adv.
